card.title: A monohybrid cross as a Punnett square

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Traits travel as discrete factors called alleles; writing the gametes on the two axes of a square and filling it shows how they recombine at fertilisation, and the square is the ratio drawn out.

figure.caption: Punnett square for Tt × Tt: 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, read as 3 tall : 1 dwarf.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Monohybrid phenotype 3 : 1, genotype 1 : 2 : 1;  dihybrid 9 : 3 : 3 : 1;  test cross 1 : 1

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Segregation and independent assortment need the genes on different chromosomes (or far apart on one), complete dominance and equally viable gametes.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Incomplete dominance gives 1 : 2 : 1 red : pink : white, codominance shows both alleles at once, and an X-linked allele appears far more often in males.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Tt × Tt gives TT, Tt, Tt, tt → 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt → 3 tall : 1 dwarf; the test cross tt × TT gives every offspring Tt.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Linked genes, epistasis, polygenic inheritance and cytoplasmic inheritance all break the neat ratios, so say so whenever a question hints at an exception.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Tt → gametes T and t → 2 × 2 squares → 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt;  T dominates, so the phenotype reads 3 : 1

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Write the gametes on the axes before filling any square, and sanity-check the ratio by its sum: 4 for one gene, 16 for two.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Work out a monohybrid cross with a Punnett square and state the phenotypic ratio obtained in the F₂ generation.
